newsitem.title: FRANCE: France halts Swiss beef imports over BSE fears.
newsitem.headline: France halts Swiss beef imports over BSE fears.

text.p: France on Friday suspended imports of live cattle and beef from Switzerland, the European country most affected by mad cow disease after Britain, Agriculture Minister Philippe Vasseur told a news conference.
Vasseur said imports were suspended from Friday and Paris would seek an early decision from the European Commission for a joint position on Swiss exports.
"This precautionary measure is taken pending the official position of the European Union," Vasseur said.
"It is justified by the absolute priority we place on protecting consumers," he added.
Switzerland has reported 230 cases of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), the most of any European country except Britain.
It has announced plans to spend some 6.5 million Swiss francs ($4.90 million) to slaughter at least 1,500 cows to eradicate the disease.
"We need to adopt a position coherent with the decisions taken by our main EU partners who have borders with Switzerland and have closed their markets to Swiss cattle," Vasseur said.
"France will do the utmost to very rapidly obtain a clear stance from the European Union on conditions for importing Swiss cattle," he said.

The European Union banned exports of British beef last March to protect public health and restore consumer confidence in beef after London raised fears that humans who ate the meat of infected animals might become ill with the brain-wasting Creuzfeldt-Jakob Disease.

Vasseur said the import of a few Swiss beef products could be authorised exceptionally under very strict sanitary conditions. But there would not be any exception to the ban on imports of Swiss cattle.
He said that in any case French imports of Swiss beef were very small. There were more French exports to Switzerland than Swiss exports to France.
